HYDROS · IIT Tirupati
Experimental forecast

Rain outlook for IIT Tirupati campus

Nested WRF model run (9 km, 3 km and 1 km grids) by the HYDROS Lab, started from GFS data of 3 Nov 2026 00:00 UTC (05:30 IST). Shown as the chance of rain in 3-hour blocks, in Indian Standard Time. This run covers 3 Nov 05:30 to 5 Nov 05:30 IST.

Please read: this is a research product, not an official forecast. The model is more useful for saying when rain may come than how much, so no rainfall amounts are shown. The chances below are model-based, not calibrated probabilities. For warnings use IMD (mausam.imd.gov.in).

Next 24 hours (campus area)

…

This run is dry until 4 Nov, then wet. The model keeps the campus area almost dry on 3 Nov and up to the early hours of 4 Nov. Rain is shown for the daytime of 4 Nov (strongest in the 14:30–17:30 IST block) and ends by the evening. A chance of rain is shown only when the model gives at least 1 mm in a 3-hour block. This page is not a cyclone forecast: cyclone Murasu crossed the Andhra coast near Ongole in the early hours of 3 Nov, about 250 km north of the campus; for cyclone and rain warnings follow IMD.

rain reported on campusfaded = still to come

Campus reports (field notes): light rain at about 20:30–20:50 IST on 24 Oct, and rain from about 14:30 to 16:00 IST on 25 Oct with some drizzle. IMD gridded rainfall for the campus cell was 0.0 mm for each day from 27 Oct to 1 Nov, and 4.8 mm on 2 Nov. Campus reports: only very light drizzle on the night of 29–30 Oct, light rain in the afternoon of 2 Nov, and no rain on 3 Nov until midday.

How to read this · limits
  • What the chance means. Each of the three model grids (9, 3 and 1 km) is checked for the share of its cells within 25 km of the campus that show rain (1 mm or more in the 3 hours; heavier rain means 7.5 mm or more). The three shares are averaged and rounded to the nearest 10 %. Levels: low under 25 %, medium 25–50 %, high 50–75 %, very high above 75 %.
  • Not a calibrated probability. The three grids come from the same starting data, so they are not independent opinions. Agreement between them is a good sign, not a guarantee. This run has not yet been checked against campus reports and IMD for the coming days.
  • Track record so far (2–3 events): the 3 km grid caught when rain started and stopped on 21 Oct and on the night of 22–23 Oct, but it also gave rain on drizzle-only days and over-estimated the amount on 22 Oct. The 9 km grid was erratic in amount (too low on 21 Oct, several times too high on 17 Oct). The 1 km grid was closest on the drizzle day but placed some rain about 10 km away. This is why amounts are not shown.
  • Last forecast check. The run of 31 Oct 12 UTC gave an 83 % chance of rain (36 % of a heavier amount) for 11:30–14:30 IST and 94 % (52 % heavier) for 14:30–17:30 IST on 2 Nov. Light rain did fall on campus that afternoon and IMD gives 4.8 mm for the day, so the timing matched, but the heavier-rain chance was too high. The runs of 27 and 29 Oct gave 0 % for the days that stayed dry. Rain amounts are not shown because the model is not reliable for them. IMD data for 3 Nov were not yet available at the time of this run.
  • The forecast is one model run from one set of starting data, and it gets less reliable the further ahead you look.
  • Coastline is approximate. Map covers 7–19°N, 73–85°E (Arabian Sea, Laccadive Sea and Bay of Bengal): the 9 km grid everywhere, with the finer 3 km grid inside the thin box around the campus.
